rulings: Capture validity: all 32 captures are valid. The new r11b-land (desktop and mobile) is a real post-landing frame: Bandit stands on a bruiser's back in the lowest water band, score 20. It shows the state but not the effects. Bandit uses the plain idle sprite with no squash, the white ring circles his waist instead of his feet (desktop r11b-land x≈620–660 y≈625–645, mobile r11b-land x≈355–425 y≈1225–1260), and the only other marks are two leftover takeoff puffs on the sand below (desktop x≈638 y≈690 and y≈750). No droplets and no gator dip.

Claims in CHANGES.md that the pixels contradict, so they get no credit: (1) 'Tall props never stand beside a row with gators.' Pines still stand in basker sand rows and overlap the gators (desktop r11-hop x≈190–260 y≈360–470 and x≈175–250 y≈640–710), and a feeding table sits under a basker's head (desktop r07-feeding x≈70–175 y≈610–720). (2) The barn's timber beams are drawn above the actors: one crosses Bandit's body (desktop r08-barn y≈720 x≈600–680, mobile r08-barn y≈1395–1420), and a heat lamp sits on a sleeper's back (desktop r08-barn x≈790 y≈490–530, mobile r08-barn x≈600–660 y≈975–1040). These are a new layering defect. Claims verified in the pixels: no sprite-box rectangles at night (desktop r10-boss, r12-endless); the boss eyeshine sits in the eye (desktop r10-boss x≈430 y≈410); the flashlight is a feathered wedge with no hard polygon (desktop r09-night); no centre-rectangle seam on any desktop land row (desktop r11-hop, r11b-land, r12-endless); an opaque header (mobile r04-pond, r07-feeding); and the Lure coin sits inside the curb footer (mobile r07-feeding).

characters (Claude 7.0, Codex 7.5): 7.5, up 0.5. Two of loop 3's three character gaps are closed in the pixels. Bandit at 1.3 tiles now holds his own against the gators (mobile r04-pond, r10-boss, desktop r09-night). The bruiser reads as its own kind: a taller knobbed back, darker hide, a broad snout and a half-shut squint (mobile r04-pond x≈320–700 y≈575–650, desktop r07-feeding x≈600–830 y≈500–545). Larger hatchlings with banded mouths read at phone size (mobile r06-nursery, desktop r07-feeding top grass row). What remains: one idle pose in every non-hop frame, the landing included (mobile r11b-land, r12-endless), and whippers share the paddler body apart from the tail. IP gate: clear. Both critics and I find no sighting. The signposts show only a painted gator and pecan (desktop r03-l1-start x≈190–265 y≈715–775).

environment (Claude 5.5, Codex 6.0): 6.0, up 0.5. Gains: the desktop centre rectangle is gone, and grass, sand and plank rows now run edge to edge at one tone (desktop r11-hop, r11b-land, r12-endless). The barn has plank side walls with posts and windows (desktop r08-barn x≈0–180 and 1100–1280). The signposts, a small boardwalk railing and the incubator crates add set dressing (desktop r03-l1-start, r07-feeding x≈110–225 y≈195–240, r06-nursery). Still short of 7: props still collide with baskers (see the claims ruling). The barn water is the same bright teal as day (desktop r08-barn, mobile r08-barn), and the barn windows are flat tan squares. The board is still flat full-width stripes split by grey concrete curbs. Portrait shows almost no props at all (mobile r04-pond, r05-whippers), and the footer is a featureless grey slab (mobile r03-l1-start y≈1520–1690).

depth (Claude 5.5, Codex 5.5): 6.0, up 0.5. In loop 3 the night gains and the new sprite-box rectangles cancelled out. Now the rectangles are gone and the night gains stand: soft nested flashlight wedges (desktop r09-night x≈560–1050), eyeshine on the eyes including the boss (desktop r10-boss), a darker falloff toward the top corners (desktop r09-night top right), and a faint warm lantern glow (desktop r09-night x≈1130–1190 y≈600–660). Basker ground shadows and swimmer waterlines still read (desktop r11-hop, r07-feeding). What holds it at 6 is a new layering defect: barn beams over Bandit and a lamp on a sleeper (desktop r08-barn, mobile r08-barn). Day and noon are lit the same (desktop r03-l1-start against r07-feeding). Curbs have no height. Basker shadows are long hard ovals that reach past the body (desktop r11-hop x≈90–430 y≈395–425). On mobile the night is close to evenly dim with no clear pool around Bandit (mobile r10-boss, r12-endless). The critics' 5.5 ignores the removal of the defect that pinned loop 3.

readability (Claude 6.0, Codex 6.0): 6.5, held. Gain: the Lure coin no longer covers hazards (mobile r07-feeding), and right-edge badges stay inside the screen (mobile r11-hop x≈1050–1100 y≈480–520). Day telegraphs stay clear, and the wider wakes help show which way swimmers travel (desktop r11b-land, mobile r11b-land). Both critics' issues hold it below 7, and I confirm them. At night the dark bruisers merge into navy water (mobile r10-boss x≈560–780 y≈790–970, desktop r10-boss x≈750–980 y≈380–480). Badges still stack (desktop r12-endless x≈75–105 y≈170–225) and sit on Bandit's head (mobile r07-feeding x≈450–510 y≈1030–1100). The top endless badge is cut off under the header, with only its pointer left (mobile r12-endless x≈140–185 y≈215–240). Swimmers in a band's two sub-lanes still overlap by about a third of a body (mobile r04-pond, desktop r05-whippers). The critics' 6.0 would be a regression the pixels do not show: no gap from loop 3 has worsened.

ui (Claude 6.5, Codex 7.0): 7.0, held; gate met. The menu, results, help and intro pixels are unchanged since loop 3 (mobile r01-title, r13-results, r15-intro), and so are the polish gaps both critics list: the 'scroll for more' pill sits on card 14's stars (desktop r02-map) and on the 'Tail rings' heading (mobile r14-help); the ring pips read like a battery; '0/4 home' is cryptic (mobile r03-l1-start); and the outlined headings are stair-stepped (r02-map, r14-help).

juice (Claude 5.5, Codex 5.5): 6.0, up 0.5. Two of loop 3's three juice gaps are fixed in the pixels. The speed strokes now trail below Bandit, behind his travel (desktop r11-hop x≈620–660 y≈710–750, mobile r11-hop). The nose wakes are now visible white wedges at phone size (mobile r11b-land x≈440–640 y≈735–890, mobile r07-feeding x≈280–330 y≈525, desktop r11b-land). Sparkles on snacks still read (desktop r10-boss, mobile r07-feeding). It does not reach 6.5: the new landing capture shows no squash, splash, droplets or dip (see the validity ruling), so contact feedback is still unproven. Steam is not visible in any gameplay still, and every non-hop frame shows the same idle pose.

mobile (Claude 6.5, Codex 6.0): 7.0, up 0.5; gate met. Three of the four blockers in loop 3's mobile ruling are fixed in the pixels. The header is opaque, with no gator art showing through (mobile r04-pond, r07-feeding, r10-boss). The Lure coin sits fully inside a curb footer, and the board ends above it (mobile r07-feeding, r03-l1-start). Right-edge badges stay inside the screen (mobile r11-hop). The board, header and footer now frame a clean portrait play space in every gameplay capture. It sits at the floor, not above it: the boss is still cropped to its head at the left edge (mobile r10-boss x≈0–215 y≈800–915); a beam crosses Bandit (mobile r08-barn); the top endless badge sits under the header (mobile r12-endless); gator heads poke over the footer's top edge (mobile r07-feeding x≈480–700 y≈1495–1515); and the footer is a large blank slab. The critics weighed the barn beam and the boss crop heavily. I count the beam under depth, where it belongs, and it does not undo three verified framing fixes.

authenticity (Claude 6.0, Codex 6.0): 6.5, held; gate met. Gains are small: the letterless gator-and-pecan signposts on every start row, the egg-incubator crates and a short boardwalk railing (desktop r03-l1-start, r06-nursery, r07-feeding). Both critics are right that the play field still reads as concrete pools more than a Hot Springs farm. No Ouachita backdrop shows in gameplay, and the baseball and bottle cap are still off-theme (desktop r08-barn, mobile r04-pond). Nothing regressed, so it holds at the gate.

Total 52.5, a new best (loop 3: 50.0). Gates met: characters 7.5, ui 7.0, mobile 7.0 and authenticity 6.5. Not met: readability 6.5 (needs 0.5 more), juice 6.0 (0.5), environment 6.0 (1.0) and depth 6.0 (1.0). Loop 5 is the last loop. Readability and juice can each reach their gate with one S fix (ranks 1–2). Environment and depth each need two half-steps, so ranks 3–6 are ordered so that one pass can land them all.

backlog.fix: Night contrast and badge layout. (a) Night gator lift: after the darkness pass, redraw each gator sprite (sprite only, so no boxes) at globalAlpha 0.3 with globalCompositeOperation='screen', or draw a 2 px cool rim (rgba(170,200,255,0.45)) by blitting the sprite offset by (0,-2) through a source-atop tint on an offscreen canvas. The backs must separate from the water in mobile r10-boss x≈560–780 y≈790–970. Halve the night water caustic alpha. (b) Badge solver: collect each frame's badge rects, sort by y, and push any overlapping badge 22 px sideways (alternating left and right). Skip the badge for any gator whose mouth is within 1 tile of Bandit, where the red footprint ring alone is enough (mobile r07-feeding). Clamp badge y to ≥ headerBottom + badgeHeight + 4 and x to [12, view.width−12−badgeWidth], with a small pointer toward the snout when clamped (mobile r12-endless top badge, desktop r12-endless x≈75–105 y≈170–225). (c) Swimmer sub-lane split: draw the float rope between sub-lanes 3 px thicker with alternating red and white floats at 1.5x size, and tint the second sub-lane 6% darker.

Make the landing read. In the landing state (the first ~120 ms after touchdown, so frames 1–4): (a) squash Bandit by drawing with ctx.translate(footX, footY); ctx.scale(1.18, 0.82), anchored at the feet so he flattens onto the back. (b) Move the impact ring to his foot line on the gator's back: a flattened ellipse 1.0 to 1.6 tiles wide and 0.35 tiles tall, a 3 px white stroke, alpha 0.85 to 0. (c) Emit 6–8 droplets as tapered arcs from the gator's waterline (the y of its scallops), not from Bandit's waist, in a light cyan with a white core. (d) Dip the gator by 3 px and widen its scallop wake for 150 ms. (e) Fade the takeoff puffs within 150 ms so they are gone by the landing frame (desktop r11b-land x≈638 y≈690/750). Update the r11b-land assertion to check the squash scale and ring y within 6 px of the foot y. Optionally give the idle a 2-frame breath bob (scaleY 1.0 to 1.03 at 1.2 s) so non-hop stills vary.

Fix the barn layering and murk the barn water. (a) Draw the timber beams in the background pass, after the lanes but before the y-sorted actors, so Bandit and the gators pass over them. Or draw them only in the margins, fading to alpha 0 across 40 px into the board. Either way, nothing may cross Bandit in desktop r08-barn y≈720 or mobile r08-barn y≈1400. (b) Draw the lamps after the actors with a 2 px cord, but choose their x from hay columns that are free of sleepers at spawn and lamp-update time (test against sleeper bounding boxes plus 0.5 tile), so no lamp sits on a back (desktop r08-barn x≈790 y≈510). Add each lamp's floor pool as a 'lighter' radial gradient, 1.4 tiles, rgba(255,170,70,0.3). (c) Barn water: fill rgba(47,90,80,0.45) over the water rows with 'multiply', and halve the caustic alpha so the water reads murky indoors. Environment gains about 0.5 from (c).

Prop placement and portrait dressing. (a) Make the tall-prop rule real. At level build, reject any prop (pine, feeding table, lantern) whose footprint row holds any actor lane (basker, sleeper or hatchling), and test its bbox against every spawn x range in that row plus 0.5 tile. Move rejected props to the margins or to empty safe rows. Desktop r11-hop x≈190–260 and r07-feeding x≈70–175 y≈610–720 must be clear. (b) Portrait dressing: on empty safe rows (start, checkpoint, grass with no actors), place 1–2 small props (cattail, stones, signpost, egg crate) inside x ∈ [16, view.width−16]. Use seeded placement away from Bandit's spawn column and the snack x positions. (c) Footer: paint the curb with a mossy top lip (a 6 px #6b8f4e strip with irregular tufts every 40–70 px) and a dark 6 px front face, and drop it to coin height + 8 px.

Zone lighting and contact shadows for day and noon. (a) Give each row a vertical linear gradient: +6% light at the top edge, −8% at the bottom. (b) Curbs: a 3 px lit top face (#e8e4da) and a 6 px dark front face (rgba(0,0,0,0.28)) below, so pens have height. (c) Shadows: replace the long hard basker ovals with a tight contact ellipse (0.9 of the body width, 6 px tall, rgba(0,0,0,0.35), blurred 3 px) plus a faint broad offset shadow. Use one light direction per zone: day offset +10 px right at alpha 0.15; noon offset 0 and shorter at alpha 0.25. (d) Zone grade: noon gets a warm 'soft-light' fill rgba(255,200,120,0.12) and day a cool rgba(180,210,255,0.08), so desktop r03-l1-start and r07-feeding no longer look the same. (e) Mobile night: increase the darkness alpha at the screen edges from about 0.55 to 0.7 so the clear pool around Bandit reads in portrait (mobile r09-night, r12-endless).

Turn the concrete pool edges into farm pen edges (procedural Canvas2D, no new paint needed). Along every water and land boundary, draw a bank strip 10–14 px tall: an irregular top edge (a seeded noise polyline), mossy stone blobs (2–4 rounded rects per 100 px in #7d7a6e and #5f6b4a with a 1 px highlight), and occasional reed tufts and roots overhanging the water by 4–8 px. Leave lane centres clear and keep the strip under the actors. Keep one plain concrete edge only in the feeding zone, where the farm uses concrete pens. In the day and noon zones, add a thin dark-green treeline silhouette with a soft haze above the den row, a stand-in for the missing Ouachita backdrop (authenticity spillover). The board must stop reading as a water park in desktop r04-pond and mobile r05-whippers.
